conventions.convention: Relative chains use mod-two coefficients and local finiteness in the ambient slice. Homology equality means that the sum of the two relative cycles is a boundary modulo ambient chains supported in the closed boundary subspace.
The Lorentzian signature is (-,+,…,+). Bulk Cauchy slices include the conformal boundary, and inextendibility is tested after increasing locally bi-Lipschitz reparameterizations.
Regulator sequences start at n=1. Renormalized entropy is assigned only when the combined sequence converges finitely in its fixed scheme; separate convergence of its summands is unnecessary.
Entropies use natural logarithms, 0 log 0 = 0, and physical units J K⁻¹. The optional cutoff-area integration uses Countable Choice and the Borel measure domain without implicit completion.

The boundary-entropy minimum is an adopted prediction for a prescribed nonempty quantum-stationary candidate class with finite values and an attained minimum. It is not identified with exact finite-cutoff microscopic entropy.

load_bearing.statement: For ambient locally finite chains a,x with boundaries supported in B, the equality [a]=[x] holds exactly when there is an ambient locally finite chain r with ∂r+a+x supported in B. The face boundary induces a differential on the quotient. The sufficient triangulated fundamental-chain construction requires the stated ambient local finiteness, incidence conditions and compact local certificates.

Assign renormalized generalized entropy exactly when the combined finite-regulator generalized-entropy sequence converges to a finite real number in its declared scheme. Quantum stationarity requires an existing zero derivative for every specified allowed candidate family.

Adopt the minimum of renormalized generalized entropy over the prescribed quantum-stationary candidates as the semiclassical boundary-entropy prediction only when the class is nonempty, the values are finite, and the minimum is attained. This prediction is not identified with exact finite-cutoff entropy.

For the prescribed two-candidate model with finite C¹ entropy branches, an isolated equality at t₀ and unequal derivatives imply that their minimum is continuous and not differentiable at t₀. These hypotheses do not force a cusp in exact finite-cutoff microscopic entropy.

concerns.concern: The Statement writes S=(1−n∂ₙ) log Tr(ρⁿ)|ₙ₌₁ without declaring a dimensionless entropy convention. Its prerequisite defines physical entropy with a factor k_B and units J K⁻¹. The displayed replica expression instead gives entropy in nats. Declare S/k_B or explicitly adopt the source's natural-unit convention here. The source formula is equation (10.4) of https://arxiv.org/html/2006.06872; its transcription does not itself establish compatibility with the local physical-unit convention.

seams_checked.note: The dictionary preserves the exact finite matrix identity's scope and nats convention, explicitly denying that it derives geometric area or the adopted minimum rule.
The dictionary limits the Noether area coefficient to the supplier's stationary hypotheses and does not extend its first law to general quantum-extremal candidates.
The AdS definition explicitly supplies a separate candidate-surface domain and borrows only the fixed-scheme and entropy-unit conventions from the null-screen supplier.
The JT postulate explicitly treats the prior dictionary as background context: its two-dimensional disk model is outside the dictionary's d≥2 domain and adopts none of its entropy assumptions.

The research-boundaries discussion retains extremization followed by minimization and the contour, saddle, cutoff and exact-state qualifications. It does not infer continuum convergence or a general GSL from the AdS minimum prescription.
